portName: Cozumel cruise piers (Punta Langosta, International Pier, Puerta Maya)
timezone: EST (UTC−5) all year; Quintana Roo does not use daylight saving time
seoTitle: Cozumel cruise port guide: piers, taxis, Chankanaab, ferry
seoDescription: Cozumel cruise port 2026: which of 3 piers you use, fixed taxi fares per cab, Chankanaab US$29, ferry to Playa del Carmen, and the US$10 Mexico cruise fee.
quickAnswer: Cozumel has three cruise piers: Punta Langosta in downtown San Miguel, and the International Pier and Puerta Maya about 4–5 km south. From the southern piers, take a licensed taxi at the posted fixed fare, priced per cab for up to four people. If you take the ferry to Playa del Carmen, aim to be back on the island two hours before all-aboard, because sailings can be cancelled in bad weather.
intro: Cozumel is one of the busiest cruise ports in the Caribbean, and on a full day several ships share the island. Which pier you get decides the day. Punta Langosta drops you in the middle of San Miguel; the International Pier and Puerta Maya, used by most big-ship lines, sit on the south-west coast close to Chankanaab and the beach clubs but a taxi ride from town. The island's draw is the water: the reefs of the west coast, Chankanaab's lagoon and the beach clubs. The ferry to Playa del Carmen is the riskiest choice you can make here.
tenderNotes: Ships normally dock. When the piers are full, some ships anchor offshore and tender passengers to Punta Langosta, downtown.

terminals.name: Punta Langosta
terminals.notes: Downtown San Miguel. You walk off the pier, over an overpass and through a shopping centre into town. Lines include Disney, MSC and NCL, among others.

terminals.name: International Pier (SSA Mexico)
terminals.notes: About 10 minutes south of town by taxi. Mainly Royal Caribbean and Celebrity. Taxi stand at the pier exit with the fare board posted.

terminals.name: Puerta Maya
terminals.notes: Just south of the International Pier, mainly Carnival Corporation lines; can take four ships at once. You cannot walk between Puerta Maya and the International Pier inside the port areas.

walkability.detail: From Punta Langosta, San Miguel is right outside the pier. From the International Pier and Puerta Maya, town is about 4–5 km north along the coast road; there is a pavement, but in heat and humidity most people take a taxi. Playa Stingray, a small beach about 1.6 km north of the southern piers, is a realistic walk.

transportSections.cost: Posted fixed fare per taxi, in US dollars, for 1–4 passengers; 5–8 passengers pay a higher rate
transportSections.time: About 10 minutes from the southern piers to San Miguel; about 5 minutes to Chankanaab
transportSections.detail: Fares are set by the island's taxi union and shown on a board at each pier's taxi stand; drivers must show the official rate card on request. Photograph the board. Fares are per cab, not per person, so share with others going the same way. Pay cash: cards are not accepted. Dollars and pesos are both taken; paying in dollars gives a worse exchange rate. At the International Pier, if the queue is long, walk out and turn left towards the El Cid La Ceiba hotel, where taxis from town drop off.

transportSections.time: A few minutes into San Miguel
transportSections.detail: Downtown shops, the waterfront promenade and the main square are within walking distance. The passenger ferry pier (Muelle Fiscal) is also downtown, opposite the end of Avenida Benito Juárez.

transportSections.cost: MX$10 per adult (as listed by the island's taxi-union information)
transportSections.detail: Shared vans run by the taxi union on set routes from Chedraui Plaza, roughly 07:00–21:00. Useful for locals; not designed for pier runs on a cruise day.

transportSections.mode: Passenger ferry to Playa del Carmen
transportSections.cost: Check fares with the operator; buy one-way tickets
transportSections.detail: Winjet, Ultramar and Xailing sail from the Muelle Fiscal downtown. Tickets are not valid on another company's boats, so buy one-way so you can catch whichever returns first. The crossing can be rough, and services are suspended in bad weather.

returnTiming.rule: Be on a taxi back to a southern pier 75 minutes before all-aboard (15:45 for a 17:00 all-aboard). From Playa del Carmen, be back on Cozumel 2 hours before all-aboard.
returnTiming.detail: The taxi ride is short, but taxi queues in town build in the afternoon when several ships leave at once. The ferry adds 35–45 minutes of crossing, plus boarding queues, plus the taxi from the Muelle Fiscal to the southern piers. A cancelled or full sailing can leave you on the mainland.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Call the port agent number in your daily programme. The ship will not wait for independent travellers. If you miss it, you pay for getting to the next port; Cozumel has an airport, and Cancún airport is reachable from Playa del Carmen. Keep your passport with you on the ferry.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: US$29 adult, US$20 child 4–12 (2026), plus taxi at the posted fixed fare

diyVsExcursion.diy: US$22 adult, US$14 child 4–12, cash only (2026), plus taxi

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Free on foot from Punta Langosta; one taxi each way from the southern piers

excursionAdvice: Most of Cozumel is easy on your own: fixed taxi fares, a park five minutes from the southern piers, beach clubs that sell day passes direct. A ship tour earns its price for Mayan sites on the mainland such as Tulum, and for any trip that relies on the Playa del Carmen ferry, because the ship waits for its own tours and not for you. Snorkel and dive trips run by established local operators are a fair alternative to ship tours, if they guarantee a return well before all-aboard.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking at Puerta Maya or the International Pier at 08:00.

steps.what: Walk off the pier, photograph the taxi fare board and share a taxi to Chankanaab (about 5 minutes).
Chankanaab: snorkel the reef from the shore, the lagoon and the botanical garden. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.
Lunch downtown, then the waterfront promenade and the main square.
Shopping or a drink near Punta Langosta. Check the time; taxi queues grow mid-afternoon.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Chankanaab park
sights.why: Reef snorkelling from the shore, a natural lagoon, botanical garden and beach, five minutes from the southern piers.
sights.tip: Entry includes loungers, hammocks and showers; snorkel gear can be rented inside or brought. Cash, Visa and Mastercard accepted. Dolphin and sea-lion programmes cost extra.

sights.name: Punta Sur eco-park
sights.why: The undeveloped southern tip of the island: lighthouse, lagoon and empty beaches.
sights.cost: US$22 adult, US$14 child 4–12, cash only (2026)
sights.tip: Farther from the piers than Chankanaab, so budget more taxi time and money.

sights.name: San Miguel waterfront and main square
sights.why: The island's only town, with the seafront promenade, shops and restaurants.
sights.tip: Walk a few blocks inland from the seafront for local prices.

sights.name: San Gervasio archaeological site
sights.why: The island's main Maya site, a sanctuary to the goddess Ixchel.
sights.cost: MX$210 for foreign visitors listed by INAH (2026)
sights.tip: Open daily 09:00–15:30, last entry 15:00. Go in the morning: there is little shade.

sights.name: Beach clubs on the west coast
sights.why: Day-pass clubs such as Paradise Beach and Mr Sanchos, with pools, loungers, food and drink.
sights.cost: Check prices on each club's own site
sights.tip: Clubs south of the piers are a short taxi ride. Confirm what the pass includes and whether drinks are extra.

sights.name: Playa Stingray
sights.why: A small free beach within walking distance of the southern piers.
sights.tip: Walk about 1.6 km north along the coast-road pavement and look for the sign and steps down.

sights.name: Playa del Carmen
sights.why: Mainland resort town across the strait, with Quinta Avenida for shopping.
sights.tip: Only on a long call and calm sea. See the return-timing rule.

beaches.name: Playa Stingray
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk north from the International Pier or Puerta Maya along the coast-road pavement.
beaches.note: Small beach reached by steps. No facilities to speak of.

beaches.name: Chankanaab
beaches.note: More snorkelling than sunbathing; the shore is rocky in places.

beaches.name: Paradise Beach and Mr Sanchos
beaches.note: Beach clubs with day passes, pools and food. Mr Sanchos sells direct rather than through cruise lines.

beaches.name: Punta Sur
beaches.howToGetThere: Taxi to the eco-park at the south of the island.
beaches.cost: US$22 adult, cash only (2026), plus taxi

food.dish: Yucatecan dishes such as cochinita pibil
Mexican classics in a garden setting

food.where: Seafront restaurants on the east coast, such as Coconuts

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming you can walk to town from Puerta Maya or the International Pier.
commonMistakes.fix: Town is 4–5 km away. Take a taxi, or plan your day around the south-west coast.

commonMistakes.mistake: Agreeing a taxi price per person.
commonMistakes.fix: Fares are posted per cab for up to four people. Photograph the board and ask to see the rate card if a quote differs.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying a return ferry ticket to Playa del Carmen.
commonMistakes.fix: Buy one-way tickets so you can take whichever operator's boat leaves first on the way back.
Be back on Cozumel two hours before all-aboard. Weather suspensions happen with little notice.
Dollars are widely accepted, but you get a worse rate and change in pesos. Carry some pesos or small dollar bills.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using ordinary sunscreen on the reef.
commonMistakes.fix: Parks ask for biodegradable, chemical-free sunscreen. Buy it before you go in the water.

safety: Cozumel is generally safe for cruise passengers, and serious incidents involving them are rare. Mexico as a whole has high levels of violent crime, and Quintana Roo, which includes Cozumel and Playa del Carmen, carries crime warnings in foreign government travel advice; check your government's current advice before you go. Use licensed taxis from the official stands, keep valuables out of sight on beaches, and drink bottled water. Strong currents run on the east coast; swim only where it is marked as safe. Hurricane season runs from June to November, and September and October are the wettest months.
scams: Taxi drivers quoting more than the posted fixed fare, or a per-person price. Check the fare board at the pier and ask for the official rate card, which drivers must carry.
Fake silver sold in jewellery shops near the piers. Look for the .925 stamp and test with a magnet: real silver is not magnetic.
Poor exchange rates when paying in dollars, with change given in pesos at a rate set by the shop. Check the posted rate first or pay in pesos.
accessibility: The piers are flat and step-free, but the walks from ship to port exit can be long, especially at Puerta Maya. Downtown San Miguel is flat with uneven pavements and high kerbs. The taxi union offers vans adapted for wheelchair users; ask at the pier stand or book ahead. Tendering, used only when the piers are full, is harder for wheelchair users. Ferries to Playa del Carmen involve steps and can be rough.
rainyDay: Rain on Cozumel usually comes in short, heavy showers, though September and October average about 250 mm a month. Snorkelling still works in light rain. The Museo de la Isla de Cozumel on the San Miguel seafront and the covered shops at Punta Langosta are the main dry options. Strong wind is the bigger problem: it can close snorkel sites and stop the Playa del Carmen ferry.
crowdTips: On busy days several ships are in port at once and taxi stands at the southern piers queue at the start and end of the day. Leave the ship early or wait half an hour after the first rush. Chankanaab and the nearest beach clubs are busiest from mid-morning. Since 1 August 2026 Mexico charges cruise passengers a US$10 fee once per itinerary (up from US$5), collected by the cruise line in taxes and fees; it rises to US$15 from 1 July 2027.

faqs.q: Which pier will my ship use in Cozumel?
faqs.a: Usually Punta Langosta (downtown) for Disney, MSC and some NCL ships; the International Pier for Royal Caribbean and Celebrity; Puerta Maya for Carnival Corporation lines. Check your daily programme, as allocations change on busy days.

faqs.q: Can I walk from Cozumel cruise port to downtown?
faqs.a: From Punta Langosta, yes; it is in town. From the International Pier and Puerta Maya, town is about 4–5 km away, so most people take a taxi.

faqs.q: How much is a taxi from Cozumel cruise port to town?
faqs.a: Fares are fixed by the taxi union and posted at each pier, priced per cab for up to four passengers in US dollars. Pay cash; pesos are also accepted.
No. Ships normally dock at one of three piers. On very busy days a ship may anchor and tender passengers to Punta Langosta.

faqs.q: Can I take the ferry to Playa del Carmen on a cruise day?
faqs.a: Yes, but it is the riskiest independent trip from Cozumel. The crossing takes 35–45 minutes, sailings stop in bad weather, and the ship will not wait. Buy one-way tickets and be back on the island two hours before all-aboard.
US$29 for adults and US$20 for children aged 4–12 on the park's official site (2026). It is about 5 minutes by taxi from the southern piers.

faqs.q: Do I need pesos in Cozumel?
faqs.a: Not strictly. US dollars are widely accepted, but change often comes in pesos and the rate favours the seller. Small bills or pesos work best.

faqs.q: Is Cozumel safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Use official taxis, watch your belongings on beaches, and check your government's travel advice for Quintana Roo before the trip.
